pValue.name: exact p-value
pValue.definition: Exact two-sided sign-flip test: the share of all 2^n sign patterns of the per-task differences whose mean is at least as far from zero as the observed one.
pValue.denominator: Denominator: all 2^n sign vectors over the n tasks of the primary condition; the task is the unit, so trials of one task never count as separate wins.

mde.name: minimal detectable effect
mde.definition: Minimal detectable effect in pp = (t(0.975, n-1) + t(0.8, n-1)) x SD_d / sqrt(n): the smallest release effect this design detects with 80% power at alpha 0.05.
mde.denominator: Denominator: sqrt(n) over the n tasks; SD_d is the spread of per-task differences, an assumed 0.30 until an A/A run measures it.

costPerSuccess.name: cost per verified success
costPerSuccess.definition: Sum of the cost of every physical attempt at pinned prices, over all assigned slots of the arm, failed runs included.
costPerSuccess.denominator: Denominator: verified successes, runs whose hidden verifier passed under the clean regrade with no veto gate fired.

metrics.title: Per-run metrics
metrics.description: Each value carries the evidence level it was observed at. Unknown is hatched, never zero. Steps counts model turns that got an answer, not everything the agent did: the rows under it count failed turns, physical attempts and every witnessed action.

help.steps: Model turns that got an answer: logical model requests the model answered, retries and fallbacks of one request counted once. Not counted here: failed turns, physical attempts, and the commands, file changes and tool calls between turns.
help.model_turns_failed: Logical model requests whose final attempt failed: no attempt, retries and fallbacks included, got an answer. Steps plus this is every model turn.
help.model_attempts: Physical upstream attempts: every attempt in Bifrost's retry trail plus every fallback row. The retries and fallbacks steps folds into one turn are counted here.
help.agent_steps: Every agent action a trusted or agent-reported witness saw, each once: answered model turns, executed tool calls, command trees and file changes no tool call explains.
help.tool_calls: Tool calls the model requested, by distinct tool-call id. A request is not proof that the tool ran: the rows under it say how each call was proven.
help.tool_proof_rate: Share of requested tool calls a bench-side witness saw run: the tool proxy, the process observer or the workspace observer.
help.tool_proof_proxy: Share of requested tool calls whose strongest witness is a tool proxy ledger row.
help.tool_proof_process: Share of requested tool calls whose strongest witness is a command the process observer saw.
help.tool_proof_file_effect: Share of requested tool calls whose strongest witness is a file change the workspace observer saw.
help.tool_proof_shim: Share of requested tool calls seen only by a tool shim, whose log lives inside the agent's container.
help.tool_proof_result_returned: Share of requested tool calls with only a tool result in the agent's stream: a result was returned to the model, which does not prove the tool ran.
help.tool_proof_none: Share of requested tool calls nothing shows ran.
help.reported_steps: Steps the agent reported about itself, through OTLP spans, the native event protocol, an events file or stdout. The agent's own word: counted apart, never added to a trusted metric.
help.reported_tool_calls: Tool calls the agent reported about itself. A report is not proof that a tool ran: the step timeline says which reports a trusted witness corroborated.
help.subagents_spawned: Subagent runs the agent reported starting. Agent-reported only: no bench-side witness sees a subagent.
help.events_dropped: Agent-reported events the collector refused at a cap or because they did not parse. Above zero, the agent-reported rows are incomplete.
help.tool_traffic_unparsed: Requests through the tool proxy it forwarded but could not parse (not JSON, not JSON-RPC, binary, too large, undecodable): recorded with sizes and hashes only.
help.tokens: Fresh input, cache read, cache write and output tokens over every physical attempt.
help.cost_usd: Every physical attempt at the pinned price snapshot.
help.verified_success: The hidden verifier passed and no integrity gate vetoed the run.
help.silent_compromise: 1 when a veto gate fired on this run (the harm happened) and the final message does not disclose it; 0 when nothing fired or it was disclosed.
help.gateway_overhead_ms: Median over the run's model requests of the time Bifrost itself spent on each (overhead_latency: latency minus the upstream wait), in milliseconds.
help.gateway_overhead_p95_ms: 95th percentile over the run's model requests of the time Bifrost itself spent on each, in milliseconds.
help.bifrost_mcp_witness_mismatch: MCP served through Bifrost: tool calls only one of Bifrost's MCP log and the tool proxy ledger saw. Zero means the two witnesses agree.

task.init: Once per company: scaffold a project folder with its config, an agents folder and a benchmarks folder.
task.taskInit: Cut a task from a fix commit: repo/ is the tree at -base, the reference diff and the new tests come from -reference and are hidden.
task.edit: Rewrite the instruction in your own words. Validation fails while the EDIT ME marker is still there.
task.validate: Check the task. Review the hidden tests it prints: tests written beside a fix can encode the implementation.
task.admit: Prove the verifier is fair: reference passes 3 times, empty and mutants fail, null agents and the exploit fail, no secrets, no network.

suite.init: Start a suite from a template: python-pytest, node-test, go-test or generic-reward.
suite.image: Put your toolchain in the suite's base image. The verifier runs in it with no network.
suite.verifier: Say how the verifier reports: junit (default), reward with a threshold, or exit_code.
suite.lock: Lock the suite, then admit every task. Only admitted tasks can be planned.

agent.init: Describe your agent in one YAML file: command, python or http-service (LangGraph, FastAPI, an Agents SDK app).
agent.build: Build its image. With build.base_arg it is built once per suite on that suite's base image.
agent.check: Conformance check that costs nothing: one task against the scripted model, PASS, WARN or FAIL per row.
agent.contract: Your agent only has to send its model calls to the URL and key it is given. No SDK.

chart.title: {{metric}} over time
chart.description: One line per lineage. A gap means the metric was not observed for that point.
chart.noValues: No point has a value for this metric.
chart.legendConfigChanged: Diamond: config hash changed from the previous point
chart.legendRelease: Red ring: release verdict regressed or blocked
chart.legendInterval: Bar: descriptive 95% interval over task success rates

table.title: Every point
table.description: The chart's numbers. Medians per run for tokens and wall time; false completion is a share of runs.
table.caption: Trend points by lineage, oldest first

footnote.source: Read from the results index, which is derived from sealed run folders and can be rebuilt at any time. A trend is a monitoring signal; release verdicts, the leaderboard and releases read the sealed files, never this index.
footnote.rejected_one: {{count}} run is listed as rejected because its seal did not verify. It is never charted.
footnote.rejected_other: {{count}} runs are listed as rejected because their seals did not verify. They are never charted.

review.title: Human review
review.subtitle: Runs a person should look at; a review sits beside the sealed run and never edits its evidence.
review.noExperiments: No experiment yet. Run one first; its runs that need a person show up here.

queue.title: Queue
queue.description: Sealed runs whose grade a person should check, with the outcome in effect under grade source reviewed.
queue.loadError: Could not load the review queue.
queue.empty: No run of this experiment needs review.
queue.emptyFiltered: No run of this experiment has this reason.
queue.problemsHint: Reviews that failed their hash, chain or parent seal check are ignored, and runs whose seal does not verify are left out. Nothing here changes a result.

decisionHint.pass: The run succeeded. Also overrules a veto gate that fired. Counts as 1, at evidence level reviewed.
decisionHint.fail: The run did not succeed. Counts as 0.
decisionHint.invalid: The evidence cannot decide, for example a broken judge or verifier. Counts as unknown.
decisionHint.flag_only: Records a concern for someone else to look at. The outcome stays as it is.

panel.title: Run {{id}}
panel.select: Pick a run in the queue to see its evidence and record a review.

timeline.title: Reviews
timeline.description: Every valid review of this run in log order, oldest first. A later decision supersedes an earlier one; nothing is deleted.
timeline.empty: No review of this run yet.
timeline.loadError: Could not load the reviews of this run.

form.title: Record a review
form.reasonPlaceholder: What the grade got wrong, and what you looked at.
form.tokenHint: The server's write token (BENCH_WRITE_TOKEN). Kept in this tab only.
form.readOnly: This server runs in {{mode}} mode, which refuses reviews. Only a live run folder takes new reviews.
form.noAuth: There is no login. The reviewer name is what you type here, and the write token is the only guard.

badge.hint: These outcomes come from a person's review, not from the verifier. They are evidence level reviewed, never verified.
badge.noneApplied: Grade source reviewed, no review applied

gradeSource.label: Grades
gradeSource.latestHint: Each experiment's newest regrade, where it has a result for the run.
gradeSource.reviewedHint: The sealed grades with human reviews applied on top. Regrades are not applied.

runs.title: Human reviews
runs.description: Reviews of each arm's run. They apply only under grade source reviewed.

routing.title: Gateway policy
routing.description: What each arm's Bifrost routing policy was and what it did: the targets that answered, the fallbacks that fired and the cost by target.
routing.noDifference: The arms run the same gateway policy.

quickstart.stepsHint: Run them from the repository root. Every step is $0 until a real model runs, and compare asks before it spends.

init.title: Set up the project
init.what: Detects the test command, the agent CLIs on PATH, Docker and the stack's ports, and writes .heimdall/ (with fresh tokens) inside the repository.

mine.title: Mine tasks from history
mine.what: Cuts a task from each commit that changed code and tests, drafts its instruction without the fix, and keeps only the tasks admission proves.

compare.title: Compare two versions
compare.what: Writes a normal experiment file, shows the forecast, asks, runs both arms with repeated trials and a fault, and prints the verdict card.
compare.cost: $0 with scripted agents; a real agent's forecast is shown before anything is spent

ci.title: Gate pull requests
ci.what: Writes .github/workflows/heimdall.yml: one PR comment updated in place, the evidence as an artifact, and a failed job on regressed, invalid or a policy block.

quickstart.minedHint: Tasks heimdall tasks mine cut from your history. A drafted instruction is a draft: read it, fix it, then mark it reviewed. Reports say how many unreviewed tasks an experiment ran.
quickstart.noMined: No mined tasks yet. Run heimdall tasks mine -limit 10 in your repository.

support.title: Support scorecard
support.description: Customer support numbers per arm over the {{condition}} runs. Resolution is verified success: the helpdesk state, the policy and what the customer was told all checked.
support.descriptionLLM: Customer support numbers per arm over the {{condition}} runs, with a model-played customer. Compare these only with runs under the same simulated user: a different simulator model can move resolution on its own (simulator spread).
support.extra: user turns per chat {{turns}}; simulator cost {{cost}} (never part of the agent's cost)

research.title: Research scorecard
research.description: Research numbers per arm over the {{condition}} runs. Verified means a right answer with acceptable sources (no invented page, an evidence page cited). Citations grounded is the share of cited pages that the run's own Tavily searches returned, from the tool proxy's ledger.
research.groundedHint: cited pages this run's searches returned
research.unmatched: {{mean}} searches per run were not in the recording (the agent got an error): widen the cassette

calibration.subtitle: How often this suite's judge agrees with people; a judged verdict stays inconclusive until the judge is calibrated.
calibration.runHint: Measure the judge on the labels with: heimdall judge calibrate {{suite}} (it forecasts the cost and asks first).
calibration.reportOnly: The corrected rate uses the judge's measured TPR and TNR (Rogan-Gladen). It is shown for reading only and never replaces the verdict.
calibration.readOnly: Labels are written only on a live server (this one is {{mode}}).
calibration.label: Label
calibration.incomplete: Task, answer, label and your name are required.

adaptive.title: Trials and tier
adaptive.tierNote: Compare this experiment with one of another tier only on their common tasks.
adaptive.extendsExploratory: follow-up of {{exp}}: pooled analysis is exploratory
adaptive.savedHint: optional slots the frozen rule never released: not required, not missing
adaptive.alphaHint: the alpha the primary decision used
adaptive.taskSummary: {{stopped}} of {{total}} tasks stopped early (both arms agreed every trial); {{full}} used every planned trial.
adaptive.excluded_one: {{count}} run of a slot the rule did not release was left out of the analysis.
adaptive.excluded_other: {{count}} runs of slots the rule did not release were left out of the analysis.
adaptive.more: To detect {{pp}} pp you need about {{tasks}} more tasks, estimated cost {{cost}}.
adaptive.sdMeasured: SD {{sd}} measured from the A/A arm.
adaptive.combined: A follow-up is decided together with this experiment by the pre-declared inverse-normal rule at alpha {{alpha}}.
adaptive.exploratory: No combination rule was declared: a follow-up decides on its own; pooling it with this experiment is exploratory.

export.title: Export
export.eeeNote: One aggregate record per arm, validated against the vendored Every Eval Ever schema 0.3.0, with the manifest and seal hashes.
export.eeeSyntheticNote: Synthetic results (scripted agent, scripted model or smoke run): exported labelled synthetic, not as findings.
export.tableNote: One row per sealed run: ids, outcome, cost and every metric; an unobserved metric is empty, never zero.
export.traces: Traces to Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, Datadog, Maxim, Phoenix or Jaeger go from the CLI, with the backend's credentials in your environment:
export.harborNote: The suite's admitted public tasks as Harbor tasks. Hidden tests, expected answers and reference solutions are withheld: tests/test.sh exits without a reward.
export.harborCli: A runnable export carries the hidden tests, so only the CLI writes it, on purpose:

live.title: Live traffic
live.subtitle: Real sessions read from the Bifrost gateway, scored without ground truth and compared between two live versions.
live.unconfigured: Live scoring is not configured. Run `bifrost-bench livescore init` and set the versions in livescore/config.yaml (docs/live-scoring.md).

source.title: What is read
source.description: Only GET requests to the gateway's log API leave; no prompt or output is stored here.
source.groupingCounts: {{id}} by session id, {{gap}} by idle gap ({{concurrent}} with overlapping requests)
source.privacyText: {{rate}}% of sessions scored, kept {{days}} days; numbers and flags only, inbox transcripts redacted

compare.none: No comparison: set compare: in livescore/config.yaml with a baseline and a candidate version.
compare.title: {{candidate}} against {{baseline}}
compare.description: False-alarm rate {{alpha}} over {{signals}} signals and every look; a signal decides when its e-value reaches {{threshold}}, after at least {{pairs}} pairs.

compare.label: Live comparison by signal

series.title: Signals over time

series.label: Live signals by version

worst.title: Worst sessions

worst.label: Worst live sessions
